turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Morning. Ned Callahan? Come through, love. Doctor's just finishing a script, so grab a seat up here.
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Thanks. He's been a bit clingy, so I'll stay right beside him.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Course. I grabbed his obs in the waiting room while he was glued to the fish. Temperature thirty-six point seven, pulse a hundred and four. All very ordinary.
[SEG0004] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He does love those fish. I was second-guessing the thermometer at home, so that's a relief.
[SEG0005] person_3 (DOCTOR): G'day, I'm Dr Patel. Sorry to keep you waiting. What's been going on with Ned?
[SEG0006] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's his ear, mainly. He's been crying in the night, and this all came on after a cold.
[SEG0007] person_3 (DOCTOR): Poor bloke. Which side are we talking about?
[SEG0008] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The right one. He keeps tugging the right ear. It started once the sniffles were easing, I think.
[SEG0009] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ned, can I ask you directly? Does your ear hurt?
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): No, Doctor. It does not hurt.
[SEG0011] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's alright. Mum, how many nights has the crying been going?
[SEG0012] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um, four nights... no, three. I nearly counted the night he just wouldn't settle for a story. It's been three nights.
[SEG0013] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the cold itself, has that finished?
[SEG0014] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The runny nose has pretty much dried up. There's still a bit of a cough, nothing dramatic. He was proper crook on the weekend, snot everywhere, sorry.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any fever in amongst this?
[SEG0016] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No fever. His gran reckoned he was hot on the lounge last night, she was quite sure, but I don't agree.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): Did you actually put a thermometer on him?
[SEG0018] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I did. It was thirty-eight... no, hang on, thirty-six point eight. I misread it. The kitchen light is hopeless.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): So a normal reading at home as well. Any gunk or discharge from the ear?
[SEG0020] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, nothing leaking out.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Vomiting? Or a sore tummy?
[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting. Tummy's fine. He's eating a bit less than usual, left half his toast, but that's it.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): What have you given him for the pain?

[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Panadol. I had the Nurofen in my hand and then I put it back, so he hasn't had any of that. The Panadol was seven and a half mils... no, six mils. The bottle says six for his age. Last night and again this morning.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): By mouth? And did it touch the pain at all?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, by mouth. He dozed for a few hours, then he was up and crying again. Sorry, his jumper's too hot in here. Not fever-hot, just your heater.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any medicines he takes all the time? Puffers, drops, anything like that?
[SEG0028] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nothing regular. He's usually a well kid. Oh, he goes to kindy Tuesdays and Thursdays, if that matters.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any allergies, to antibiotics in particular?
[SEG0030] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I don't think so. Well, actually, long ago he had a course of amoxicillin. He got a rash, maybe. I'm not sure it was from the medicine.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Can you place when that was, or what the rash looked like?

[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I can't date it. He was little, maybe around one, I honestly don't know. It might have been a viral rash. Gran says one thing, I remember another, and I never wrote it down.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Alright. I'll treat amoxicillin as a possible allergy for now, and I won't be using it today. We can untangle that story another time.
[SEG0034] person_4 (PATIENT): Excuse me, Doctor.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Yes, Ned, go on.
[SEG0036] person_4 (PATIENT): I was mistaken earlier. My ear does hurt. It hurts when I lie down at night.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that's really helpful. I thought Mum might be onto something. May I look in your ears with the little light?
[SEG0038] person_4 (PATIENT): Yes, please. If you would be gentle.
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Gentle as I can. The right eardrum is a bit pink. It's not bulging, and I can't see a fluid level. The left ear looks clear. Throat's not red either, while I'm looking.
[SEG0040] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So do you reckon it's an infection?

[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm thinking out loud, so stop me if I rush. It might be an early middle-ear infection, or it might just be the ear aching as the cold settles, because the drum isn't really bulging, and I can't honestly pick one for certain. He's not feverish and he doesn't look toxic, so I reckon we watch and wait rather than start an antibiotic this morning.
[SEG0042] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Even with him crying half the night? I barely slept, and I've got a shift tomorrow, which is my problem, not his.

[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): The night crying fits the ear pain. Keep going with the Panadol, six mils, up to four times in a day. Don't add ibuprofen on top unless you've checked with us. Just the paracetamol.
[SEG0044] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Six mils, up to four times. Should I send him to kindy tomorrow? He usually goes Thursdays, and tomorrow's Thursday.
[SEG0045] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep him home tomorrow and see how the night goes. It's just you and his gran at home, isn't it?
[SEG0046] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes. Gran minds him when I'm at work. She'll fuss, but she'll follow what you say.

[SEG0047] person_3 (DOCTOR): If he is not better in two days, bring him back. Sooner than that if a fever actually starts, or the ear starts discharging, or the pain is really bad. We'll make an antibiotic plan then, and it won't be amoxicillin.
[SEG0048] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no script to take away today? The backup is just to come back?
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): No script today. If it hasn't settled when I see him again, I might use cefalexin, but I'm not starting that now. I want another look first.
[SEG0050] person_4 (PATIENT): May I get down now, please?
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Nearly, mate. Is your throat sore at all?
[SEG0052] person_4 (PATIENT): No, thank you. My throat is not sore.
[SEG0053] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Mum, any dizziness, or do you think his hearing has dropped?
[SEG0054] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No dizziness. Hearing seems normal. He answers when I call from the kitchen, usually to tell me he is busy.
[SEG0055] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Sorry, just sticking my head in. Want me to book a review at the desk?
[SEG0056] person_3 (DOCTOR): No fixed appointment. Only if he's not better in two days, Mum can ring and we'll squeeze him in.
[SEG0057] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll ring if we need you. Thanks for explaining it. I was bracing for a fight about antibiotics.
[SEG0058] person_3 (DOCTOR): No worries. You're already doing the sensible stuff. Ned, you were very polite.
[SEG0059] person_4 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. Goodbye.
[SEG0060] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): I'll walk you back out. Mind the step, Ned.

spec.situation: Mother and a child with ear pain and night crying after a cold; mother says no fever, grandmother says it was hot; mother unsure about the amoxicillin the child had 'long ago, got a rash maybe'; doctor decides on watchful waiting with a back-up plan.
features: self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.

denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

bad.reason: Right ear pain after sniffles easing and worse lying at night supported, but pain was reported by patient, not family member.
bad.text: Right ear pain (category=ENT, status=present, onset=after the sniffles were easing, temporality=current, body_site=right ear, aggravating_factors=lying down at night, reported_by=family_member, certainty=certain)

bad.reason: Transcript mentions a past course of amoxicillin, not a discontinued current medication.

omissions.text: Initial direct patient statement denying ear pain was recorded wrongly/omitted: Ned first said his ear did not hurt, then later corrected himself that it does hurt, especially when lying down at night.
No regular medicines: mother said he takes nothing regularly, including no puffers or drops.
Doctor documented/planned to treat amoxicillin as a possible allergy for now and specifically said he would not use amoxicillin today.
No antibiotic prescription was given today; backup plan is to return/review rather than take away a script now.
Follow-up logistics: no fixed appointment was booked; if not better in two days, mother should ring and they will squeeze him in.
